blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
English comes in CAN's, not in CAN'Ts. Taxes can sound hard, but in English they follow simple patterns. Today you learn five useful words and practise them in short, easy sentences.

Sophie works on the fiscal team. She helps the student write a short thank-you email to the accountant. She says the polite words slowly: thanks, please, sorry, welcome, appreciate. "Go slowly," she says. "One step at a time."

The email is short. It says thank you for the help with the tax form. It says please one time, and it is polite. Sophie smiles. "Good job. Now you are ready for the next tax topic."

items.q: Who helps the student write the email?
items.why: "Sophie works on the fiscal team. She helps the student write a short thank-you email."

items.q: What is the email about?
options: Saying thank you for help with the tax form
items.why: "It says thank you for the help with the tax form."

items.q: How many useful words do you learn today?
items.why: "Today you learn five useful words."

items.q: "English comes in CAN's, not in CAN'Ts." This suggests that Sophie wants the student to feel…
items.why: Inferência: a frase é uma mensagem positiva — foco no que você PODE fazer, para dar confiança.

items.q: The text suggests that Sophie would most likely AGREE that…
options: taxes are too hard to learn in English
small, slow steps make learning easier
learning English should be fast and stressful
polite words are not important in emails
items.why: Inferência: "Go slowly. One step at a time" mostra que ela valoriza passos pequenos e calmos.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Sophie ajudando o aluno a escrever o e-mail. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Hi. My name is Sophie. I work on the fiscal team here at Czarnikow. Today we write a short email to the accountant. Are you ready? Good. Let's start.

The accountant helped us with the tax form last week. It was a big help. So now we say thank you. In English, we can write: "Thank you for your help." It is short and it is polite. We do not need long words. Short is good.

We also use the word please. For example: "Please send me the new form." Please makes the email kind. And if we make a small mistake, we say sorry. For example: "Sorry for the late reply." These words are easy, but they are very important. They help people feel good.

Now, read the email one more time. Is it polite? Yes. Is it short? Yes. Good job. I appreciate your work today. Really, thank you. You are welcome to ask me any question. Next week, we learn more tax words. Go slowly. One step at a time. You can do it.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: Where does Sophie work?
options: On the fiscal team at Czarnikow
items.why: "I work on the fiscal team here at Czarnikow."

items.q: Why do they write "thank you" to the accountant?
options: Because he is the new manager
Because he helped with the tax form
items.why: "The accountant helped us with the tax form last week… So now we say thank you."

items.q: Which word do we use when we make a small mistake?
items.why: "if we make a small mistake, we say sorry."

items.q: Sophie says the words are easy, "but they are very important." This suggests that…
options: small polite words still matter a lot
you should not use polite words
items.why: Inferência: mesmo simples, as palavras educadas fazem diferença — por isso ela as destaca.

items.q: How would you best describe Sophie's tone?
items.why: Inferência: "Good job… You can do it… One step at a time" mostra um tom gentil e encorajador.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "Thanks for your help with the tax form." Thanks means…
items.why: Thanks = obrigado(a). É a forma curta de "thank you".

items.q: Choose the correct word: "___ send me the new form today."
items.why: Please = por favor. Usamos para pedir algo de forma educada.

items.q: "Sorry for the late reply." Sorry means…
items.why: Sorry = desculpa. Usamos quando cometemos um erro pequeno.

items.q: Someone says "thank you." You reply: "You're ___."
items.why: You're welcome = de nada. É a resposta educada a um "thank you".

items.q: "I really appreciate your work today." To appreciate means to…
items.why: Appreciate = valorizar / agradecer. Mostra que você reconhece o esforço do outro.

blocks.instruction: Expressões educadas que aparecem em e-mails de trabalho. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "Thank you for your help with the form." This is a polite way to…
options: say you are thankful for something
items.why: Thank you for + algo = agradecer por algo específico. Muito comum em e-mails.

items.q: "I will get back to you tomorrow." This means I will…
items.why: Get back to you = retornar / responder depois. Comum quando você não pode responder agora.

items.q: "Please reach out if you have a question." To reach out means to…
items.why: Reach out = entrar em contato, procurar alguém para falar.

items.q: "I will follow up next week about the tax form." To follow up means to…
items.why: Follow up = dar continuidade, checar de novo mais tarde.

items.q: "I look forward to your reply." This means I…
options: am waiting happily for your answer
items.why: Look forward to = aguardar com expectativa. Fecho educado e positivo de e-mail.
